GND: common with PSU1 V- and PSU2 V-
Grove stick: lower rail, left stick
Grove stick: lower rail, right stick
Grove stick: upper rail, left stick
Grove stick: upper rail, right stick
Grove stick: CLOSED light, behind the plate
1-6 C A S I N O, 7-10 N E P O (reversed)
arrow direction: handle on the GND side

casino closed: handle on the GND side = LOW =
CLOSED (OPEN letters off, CLOSED light on);
handle on the other side = casino open

USB-B cable (upload, Serial Monitor): ONLY while PSU1 (5 V) is
switched OFF. PSU1 feeds the Mega 5V pins (the sticks get their
power through the Grove shield), so with USB plugged in as well
two 5 V sources would be connected together. Switch PSU2 off too.
Total: 28 pixels (84 LEDs) in 2 WS2811 12 V strips plus 11 Grove sticks with 10 LEDs each (10 arrow sticks + the
1. Two supplies: PSU1 (LRS-50-5, 5 V) feeds the Mega 5V pins (both), the Grove shield, the sticks and the LCD;
PSU2 (LRS-50-12, 12 V) feeds ONLY the two strips. Never connect +12 V to an Arduino pin or to the 5 V parts.
2. Common ground: PSU1 V-, PSU2 V-, Arduino GND (and the shield) and the GND of both strips and all sticks are
3. D11 = frame strip, 18 pixels, pixel 1 in the lower-left corner, counter-clockwise (front view): 1-6 bottom,
7-9 right going up, 10-15 top right to left, 16-18 left going down. Feed +12 V at the start and the end.
4. D12 = letters strip, 10 pixels (one per letter): 1-6 C A S I N O, then 7-10 N E P O. OPEN is wired in reverse
order on the strip; the program maps the letters. D13 stays the status LED.
5. Put each 330 ohm resistor close to the first pixel of its strip. Keep data wires short. The sticks plug
straight into the Grove shield (no resistors, no wire from a supply).
6. The Mega's 5 V data signal into a 12 V WS2811 strip normally works (as in the strip tests) but is not
verified for the final sign; the 74HCT125 buffer is listed as insurance.
7. SW6 (program, absolute): pins 1, 2, 4, 8 go to D34-D37, C to GND; position 0..E = program 0..14, F = random.
SW3 (menu, relative): pins 1, 2, 4, 8 go to D42-D45, C to GND; a change of the code is a step (1..7 forward,
9..15 back). A position counts in binary (0..F). If your switch gives the complement (15 - position), set
8. All inputs (SW1, SW2, SW3, SW5 to SW9) use the internal pull-ups (INPUT_PULLUP), so no resistors are needed
for them. Speeds and brightness curves are menu properties (saved in EEPROM); the old speed switches SW3/SW4
9. CLOSED (the 11th Grove stick, 10 white LEDs, shield connector A0) sits BEHIND the plate under the CLOSED hole
text and is lit only while SW5 says closed.
10. LCD1 (I2C backpack) uses the Mega's I2C pins D20 (SDA) and D21 (SCL) plus the Mega 5V and GND pins (about 30
11. Arrow sticks: the 10 Grove RGB LED sticks go into the Grove Base Shield connectors D2-D8 and A1-A3 (A0
carries the CLOSED light stick; the connector of each stick is listed in the data rows above; the shield's
3V3/5V switch must be on 5 V). Connect the +5 V bus to BOTH 5V pins of the Mega's long header and the GND
bus to the Mega GND pins, as in stick_test_direct (tested on real hardware).
12. Pin 13 (the LED on the Mega board) blinks while the program runs; the Serial Monitor (115200 baud) shows one
